dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The 31-May cluster contains 17 annual records (`term_days = 365`): 8 from DLR-104 and 9 from DLR-219"
"The May annual records reconcile to the dealer import log: DLR-104 = 8 rows / $723.42 and DLR-219 = 9 rows / $782.87"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "These 17 records were posted in the same 21:00 batch, but their `effective_event_date` values are spread from 1–28 May"
"The operations explanation matches the observed batch pattern: annual files are submitted monthly while dealer transaction dates are retained as effective dates"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Material Unknowns"
"The current support is operational explanation rather than the underlying dealer agreement or process control"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Keep the postings unchanged and run one targeted check: recalculate the flagged renewal trend using `effective_event_date` and compare it with the `posted_at` trend."
"Revenue-recognition basis: The data shows posting and effective dates but does not prove whether annual revenue is recognized immediately or over the subscription term."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Do not escalate or reverse the 31-May postings."
"This is reversible and will show whether the apparent month-end spike is only a reporting-timestamp effect."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Duplicate revenue: Rejected because the 17 records have unique `recharge_id` and `source_event_id`, and their dealer-level counts and values reconcile to the import log." Unique identifiers and import-log reconciliation do not by themselves test duplicate cash collection or duplicate customer entitlement.

"Pipeline defect: Rejected because the cluster reconciles to the dealer import records and the pattern matches the documented monthly batch process." This is stronger than the evidence supports because an upstream or downstream defect could still preserve those file-level counts and values.

"Do not escalate or reverse the 31-May postings." The no-reversal recommendation is reasonable, but no direct cash-ledger or entitlement-level duplicate check is shown, so the unconditional no-escalation conclusion is somewhat premature.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst considered duplicate revenue, period stuffing, and pipeline defect, but missed the strongest residual alternative: distinct recharge IDs could still represent duplicate cash charges or duplicate annual entitlements for the same customer/account. File-level row and value reconciliation would not detect that without customer, contract, entitlement, or cash-ledger joins.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run explicit duplicate cash and entitlement checks by customer/account or contract, joining the 17 records to the payment ledger and active entitlement/subscription records; verify both duplicate amounts and duplicate service periods before making the no-escalation conclusion unconditional.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South June cases were 104 (index 59), while controls remained near baseline; pre-auth termination was 24.0% under NOVA versus 7.9% under South LEGACY; South outages remained steady."
"382 June pre-auth sessions produced no `case_id`; across NOVA, 464 failed pre-auth sessions came from 411 subscribers"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The South case decline is not clean evidence of better customer experience because the pilot introduced both genuine self-service and a measurement/authentication path that prevents many failed contacts from becoming CareDesk cases."
"CAUSAL CLAIM (tentative): Authentication/prompt failures and changed case creation caused part of the decline, while new self-service caused some genuine improvement."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "INFERENCE: Part of the complaint decline is hidden deflection because failed pre-auth sessions do not enter CareDesk."
"All improvement is fake. Rejected because NOVA introduced new `balance_check` and `pack_info` self-service stages that were absent from LEGACY."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NOVA-S1 nationally yet."
"Run one targeted query linking South subscribers with an authentication error to any support contact or callback within the next 7 days."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "What changed from LEGACY to NOVA in the conditions for creating a CareDesk case, transferring to an agent, or resolving-and-closing a contact?"
"What like-for-like metric and control-region comparison must be passed over two complete weeks before national expansion is approved?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Authentication/prompt failures and changed case creation caused part of the decline" is a plausible and appropriately tentative causal claim, but the submission does not directly show the pre/post case-creation rule change or establish that the no-`case_id` sessions were complaints.

"new self-service caused some genuine improvement" is not directly demonstrated by the presence of `balance_check` and `pack_info` stages; successful resolution or reduced repeat contact is still unknown.
"controls remained near baseline" is asserted from June counts, but the supporting baseline period or a reproducible regional time-series comparison is not shown.
The submission does not cite or explicitly use the rollout email's metric exclusions, a material source expected for validating the containment interpretation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative: some of the reduction may be real because NOVA added self-service journeys absent from LEGACY. It also preserved the possibility that failed authentication contacts were recovered or resolved through callbacks or later support, but it did not fully test whether abandonment represented dissatisfaction versus non-complaint IVR activity.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a reproducible linked-journey analysis, with explicit cohort definitions and pre/post control comparisons, showing whether South subscribers experiencing authentication errors later made repeat contacts, received recovery actions, or achieved successful resolution; pair this with sampled call listening.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv` and specific fields for the four rows, dates, inverter IDs, `impact_mw`, `cleared`, severity, and duration.

It explicitly distinguishes the observed 4/4 zero-impact values from the inference that the field might be defaulted: “zero impact should not be over-interpreted until the field is confirmed as actively populated rather than defaulted.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It cross-checks multiple event attributes—zero impact, cleared status, severity, duration, recurrence, and distinct inverters—rather than relying only on event names.
It tests a plausible innocent explanation by asking whether the export is complete or filtered, but it does not triangulate an independent operational channel beyond this CSV.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission uses claim-specific confidence levels and states that the extract “does not state whether this is the complete plant export or a filtered slice.”
It identifies the smallest decision-changing check: confirm the export date filter and total plant event count, while also qualifying the constant-zero `impact_mw` field.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation—“run one cheap completeness check first”—is reversible and proportionate to four short, cleared, zero-impact events.
The conditional stopping rule, “if it is, stop here,” avoids unnecessary escalation while preserving a check for an incomplete export.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately scopes the result to “this file” and says it shows “no recorded impact, open event, or recurring pattern,” rather than asserting that no plant issue could exist.
It follows the supplied evidence and does not invent a plant problem from communications or other warning text.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Do not escalate any of the 4 events” is reasonable for the supplied records, but it remains conditional on the completeness check and on the event fields being trustworthy; the submission appropriately states those conditions.

“No recurrence” is supported only within the four-row extract, not necessarily across the plant or a longer period; the submission generally scopes this to the extract but could state that limitation more prominently.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The extract could be incomplete or filtered, or `impact_mw` could be a defaulted/unpopulated field; under that interpretation, the absence of recorded impact and recurrence would not yet rule out a material event. The proposed completeness check directly addresses this alternative.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: After confirming export completeness, verify the provenance/population logic for `impact_mw`—or cross-check it against plant telemetry or an independent production/availability record—because all four values are identically zero.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies the 28-May and 29-May totals and states that the 31.6% calculation reproduces from `dispatch_blocks.csv` and the impact note.
It gives the same-day figures from `base_schedule_mw` and `submitted_schedule_mw`: Rs 549,664 versus Rs 453,086 across all 96 blocks on 29 May.
It distinguishes DSM penalty from net commercial value using the Rs 2.72/kWh energy valuation in `DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf`.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly tests the key alternative explanation that different day-level conditions drive the headline result: “31.6% is a cross-day comparison.”
It cross-checks another day and firmware context: “A conventional 4-Jun day had a lower penalty ... but it used firmware 4.8 rather than 4.7.”

It also identifies a plausible causal limitation by asking whether the 12 revisions were generated before actual generation was known. The reasoning is strong, but it does not fully establish that the base schedule is a valid operational no-pilot counterfactual or quantify other day-level confounders.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly limits the estimate: “The 17.5% is a same-day counterfactual estimate, not an observed before-versus-after result.”
It states that generality beyond 29 May, ex-ante timing, and net commercial value remain unknown.
It avoids both overclaiming and overcorrecting: “do not scale it yet” while retaining the approximately 17.5% same-day benefit.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to “Keep the current pilot unchanged and do not scale it yet” follows from one positive but unreplicated same-day estimate and incomplete net-value evidence.
The proposed “targeted read-only query across additional high-wind days” is reversible and directly tests whether the within-day effect repeats.
The action preserves the legitimate observed signal rather than recommending either immediate expansion or termination.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately separates the arithmetically correct 31.6% cross-day observation from the approximately 17.5% same-day counterfactual estimate.
It meets the central requirement to recognize that the pilot day performed better without asserting that the pilot caused a 31.6% reduction.
It appropriately scopes the result to one pilot day, DSM penalty, and unresolved commercial value.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The defensible estimate is a same-day counterfactual reduction” is appropriately qualified, but the submission could more explicitly state that validity depends on `base_schedule_mw` representing a credible no-pilot schedule and on revisions being ex ante.
“28 May is the highest-penalty day in the file” is traceable to the cited daily totals, but the submission does not show the full daily comparison table.

The statement that actual generation being available when revisions were made would “invalidate” the forecast-skill causal claim is somewhat strong; it would undermine that mechanism and require a different explanation, but would not necessarily invalidate all schedule-effect evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot may have reduced DSM penalties on 29 May, but the apparent benefit could partly reflect a non-comparable operational context or revisions informed by information unavailable to the intended ex-ante process. Conversely, the lower same-day penalty is still evidence of potential value and should not be dismissed merely because the 31.6% cross-day comparison is invalid for causal attribution.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify revision timestamps against the availability of actual generation and recompute the same base-versus-submitted comparison across multiple comparable high-wind STOW days, including net energy settlement value.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Declared `90211000` is the approved Swiss code for P1001, effective 2025-01-01 and current on the 2025-11-04 entry date" — tied to `country_tariff_matrix.xlsx` and `declaration.pdf`.
"Flagged `90211090` is P1001's Helios commodity code" — tied to `review_note.txt` and `product_master_current.xlsx`.
"The EU code changed from `90211010` to `90211090` on 2025-07-01" — tied to effective-date rows in `country_tariff_matrix.xlsx`.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Do not escalate the `90211000` vs `90211090` mismatch as a broker declaration error."
"Rejected because `90211000` is the Swiss-approved code for P1001 on the declaration date."
"Helios `90211090` matches the EU CN8, while the matrix states Switzerland uses a Swiss local tariff code and cross-jurisdiction string matching is ‘not expected’."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The evidence table assigns "High" confidence to each listed claim.
"The canonical schema does not model code-system identifier, nomenclature version, or effective dates" appropriately identifies a material data limitation.
"a separate quantity/value inconsistency" identifies another issue, but the submission does not state how that uncertainty affects the overall decision or what would verify it.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "both share HS6 `902110`, making this a cross-code-system false positive" explains the mechanism of the mismatch.
"The canonical schema does not model code-system identifier, nomenclature version, or effective dates" connects the finding to system design and data lineage.
"The EU code changed from `90211010` to `90211090` on 2025-07-01, showing that code comparison is also effective-date dependent" identifies the temporal mechanism.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not escalate the `90211000` vs `90211090` mismatch as a broker declaration error" is proportionate to the documented jurisdiction/code-system mismatch.
The submission separately flags "a separate quantity/value inconsistency" rather than treating every anomaly as the same code issue.
It does not, however, recommend a concrete, proportionate follow-up for the quantity/value inconsistency or specify a reversible validation step before closing the case.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Calling the mismatch definitively "a cross-code-system false positive" is reasonable but slightly stronger than the cited summary because the submission does not show the actual comparison rule execution or exact flagged-event record.

The evidence table says the invoice has "Qty 10 but line value = unit value = CHF 126,900" and the AWB shows "4 pieces," but it does not establish whether the invoice field labels, packing structure, or shipment aggregation make this an actual error.
The rejected-hypothesis section is incomplete in the supplied submission, ending with "Rejected because Helios is com", so the full basis for rejecting that hypothesis is not available.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The code mismatch is benign, but the transaction may still require separate review because the invoice records quantity 10 while the AWB records 4 pieces and the invoice's line value equals its unit value at CHF 126,900. That could reflect a genuine quantity/value or document-structure problem, even though it does not support treating the Swiss tariff code as a broker declaration error.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete the hypothesis-testing section and add exact row/event citations plus a narrowly scoped follow-up for the invoice/AWB discrepancy, including verification of invoice field semantics and shipment aggregation before closure.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The available SUP-02/P1006 Irish supplier declaration expired on 2025-07-31, before the declaration date of 2025-09-18" and cites `supplier_declaration_reference.txt` and `declaration.pdf`.
"The register search found no current document reference for SUP-02/P1006 on 2025-09-18" and identifies the specific source `supplier_declaration_reference.txt`.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission explicitly rejects "US manufacturing origin proves the preference claim is false" because the workshop states Helios was "not designed to prove preferential origin."
It also rejects "No current register reference proves no valid supplier declaration exists" using both the register limitation and the workshop evidence that documents may be outside the register.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The claim is unsupported, but it is not proven false because the supplier-document register may be incomplete."
"Unknown: whether a current supplier declaration exists outside the register" and "Unknown: whether SUP-02 was the actual supplier for this shipment."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains that "supplier declarations may sit in category folders and the register is not always updated when sourcing routes change."
It distinguishes manufacturing data from preferential-origin evidence: "Helios manufacturing country was not designed to prove preferential origin."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold the preference claim and perform one reversible evidence check" rather than declaring fraud or definitively rejecting the claim.
"Do not clear the preference claim until that evidence and the rule supporting it are identified," while recognizing that "the unresolved preference claim is duty-neutral for this line."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: No material unsupported or overstated claim is apparent. The submission appropriately frames the claim as unsupported on the available evidence rather than false or fraudulent.
The statement that the line is duty-neutral depends on the cited 0.0% rate remaining applicable, but the submission limits that statement to the line and does not use it to validate origin.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A current, valid supplier declaration may exist in supplier or category folders outside ClearView and the register, possibly for a supplier other than SUP-02. If it covers P1006, the shipment date of 2025-09-18, and the applicable preference rule, the claim could be eligible despite the expired declaration and US manufacturing-country data.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quote or extract the controlling preference rule and verify the actual shipment supplier, then trace those facts to a current supplier declaration and its covered dates and products.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Receipt→release gives mean 45.5 h / median 39.4 h, while the SOP-defined evidence→release clock gives mean 26.9 h / median 21.3 h" — cites specific fields and SOP language, distinguishing the two clocks.
"185/262 rows (70.6%), or 185/220 rows with a release timestamp (84.1%), are stamped exactly 02:10:00" — provides row-level counts and triangulates batch data with source freshness.
"42 HOLD rows have no qcore_release_ts ... all 220 dispositioned rows were received on or before 20-Jul" — identifies the cohort and missingness pattern supporting the selection-bias concern.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The current extract can produce materially different cycle-time results depending on the clock and population" — separates clock definition and population effects from the headline KPI.

"Rejected because that result uses the receipt clock rather than the SOP's evidence-available clock, includes exception work, and is heavily affected by the 02:10:00 snapshot timestamp" — builds a multi-factor causal explanation rather than treating the anomaly as a single cause.

"real intraday disposition times would weaken the artifact concern, while different live times would confirm that the extract timestamp is a snapshot default" — identifies an observation that would discriminate competing mechanisms.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The evidence table assigns claim-specific confidence levels, including "Medium" for the CertVault interpretation rather than asserting a control breach.
"The exact definition of qcore_release_ts was not verified" and "the extract alone cannot establish a control breach" — explicitly identifies consequential uncertainty.
The submission bounds the KPI impact with alternative medians (21.3 h versus 8.4 h and 5.5 h for a narrower population), though it does not fully reconcile extract snapshot timing across all sources.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Yes, it smells; do not ship the QC cycle-time KPI yet" — directly changes the publication decision.
"The smallest decisive verification is to confirm what qcore_release_ts means" — proposes a focused, reversible next action instead of broad analysis.
"publishing 'about a day and a half' as a KPI would turn a measurement artifact into a target" — identifies the operational second-order risk and links it to the recommendation.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission rejects the strongest performance interpretation: "QC release reliably takes about a day and a half," using clock, exception-population, and timestamp evidence.
It tests and rejects "The timestamps are simply corrupted" using "no negative durations" and "no lab-complete-before-receipt records."
It states what could revive the alternatives: live intraday timestamps, eventual completion of the HOLD cohort, and reconciliation of CertVault statuses to underlying certificates.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "checking the data catalog and spot-checking 5–10 rows stamped exactly 02:10:00 in live QCore" — requests a small, high-value verification tied directly to the key ambiguity.

"An approved definition specifying evidence→disposition, eligible dispositions, treatment of complex exceptions, and treatment of open HOLD work" — identifies the minimum governance decision needed for a valid KPI.
"CertVault statuses were not reconciled to the underlying certificates" — requests a targeted reconciliation rather than generic additional data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "the QCore daily snapshot boundary" is a plausible interpretation of the 02:10 concentration, but the submission has not yet verified that qcore_release_ts is a snapshot commit/default rather than a genuine disposition timestamp.

The statement that all 42 HOLD rows "have not yet had time to reach disposition" is directionally supported by the newest receipt cohort, but it is an inference from extract timing rather than proof that no disposition occurred outside the extract or that the cohort is comparable.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 concentration could be a legitimate operational release window or a real disposition time rather than an interface artifact; in that case, the long cycle time may reflect genuine workflow delay. This remains open until the data catalog and event-level or live-QCore timestamps establish the semantics of qcore_release_ts.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain the field definition and a small event-level reconciliation for 5–10 02:10 rows, including evidence-available, decision/disposition, and interface-commit timestamps, while aligning QCore and LabTrack to the same snapshot. This would distinguish workflow delay from interface timing before any KPI is published.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "8 requests are clean matches worth about $20,536"
"11 requests lack a manufacturer part number"
"HA-0022 and ME-0006 show positive on-hand stock despite negative global availability"
"All VLV-3722 stock is rev B while some requests require rev A"
"Servo-drive stock is reserved for a safety-critical asset"

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "A search hit is only a candidate; transfer requires matching manufacturer part number, revision, qualification and genuinely free stock."
"Negative global availability means no stock exists — rejected because some locations show positive on-hand stock and global availability can lag reservations."
"Same part family means interchangeable — rejected because revision differences and site-specific qualification can block transfer."

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "8 requests are clean matches worth about $20,536" with confidence "High"
"8 requests with identity/qualification/revision gaps ... Needs check"
"Live local stock confirmation could resolve the negative-availability cases."

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Transfer only 8 requests now, place 12 requests in needs-check, and keep buying externally for 4 requests."
"A search hit is only a candidate"
"Engineering confirmation ... and receiving-site qualification could clear some conditional matches."

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Every search hit should be transferred" — rejected because identity, revision, qualification and truly-free stock must all be confirmed.
"Negative global availability means no stock exists" — rejected because some locations show positive on-hand stock
"Reserved servo drives can be moved" — rejected because they are reserved for safety-critical equipment.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A confirmed manufacturer part number could move identity-uncertain requests forward."
"Live local stock confirmation could resolve the negative-availability cases."
"Engineering confirmation of VLV-3722 rev A/B interchangeability and receiving-site qualification could clear some conditional matches."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The "8 requests" and "$20,536" are presented as high-confidence actionable value without showing row-level quantities, prices, or the specific restriction checks supporting each request.

"Actionable now" is stronger than the evidence supports if the global MaintStar or stock extracts are stale or not point-in-time coherent; the submission requests live confirmation only for some cases.

The explanation that negative global availability "can lag reservations" is plausible, but the submission does not establish whether lag, reservations, timing mismatch, or another reconciliation issue caused the observed discrepancies.

The four servo-drive requests are classified as "Not transferable," although the submission itself says transfer could occur if the safety-critical reservation were formally released; "blocked pending release" would be better calibrated.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent eight clean matches may be semantic candidates rather than currently transferable stock. Because enterprise extracts may reflect different timestamps, local on-hand, reservations, global availability, and maintenance demand could be inconsistent; the correct immediate action may therefore be to hold all transfers pending a current reservation and availability check, while still using the search results for candidate generation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add a row-level decision ledger for every proposed transfer, including request ID, manufacturer part number, revision, UOM, qualification, quantity, local free quantity, reservation/criticality status, source timestamp, and receiving-site confirmation; then reclassify "transfer now" only after a current MaintStar/reservation snapshot confirms those fields together.
